evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never frames the 10–15 minute time box or promises a dependable quote. Jumps straight from 'Let me make sure we have availability' into scheduling.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Customer's concerns about size and complexity of move surface organically ('this would in essence be a two place pickup'), but rep never asks 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' or explicitly discovers what they want answered on the call.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives hourly rate ($190/hr for 3 movers + $140 trip fee) and minimum ($615 for 2.5 hrs) but does not anchor to a typical range for a home this size, nor does he personalize to this customer's stated complexity (two pickups, first-floor-to-second-floor, furniture-only, gated community). Pricing is bare-bones.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee disclosed ($140), hourly rate explained ($190), but no 'not a guess' framing, no 2.5-hour minimum explanation tied to a commitment, no 15-minute-increment transparency. Fee disclosure is present but weak on the confidence/commitment side.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Customer says 'I'm gonna have to discuss this with my husband and get back to you' — rep accepts this without ever asking 'Does that feel fair?' or holding space for reaction.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep says 'No problem feel free to give us a call with when you're ready to schedule' — this is a passive hand-off with a built-in out (call us back), not 'Would you like our help with your move?' asked plainly.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking confirmed at all. Customer defers to discuss with husband; rep does not secure date, phone, arrival window, crew size, or move notes. Call ends with customer saying they'll call back.

top_strength: Jules gathered extremely thorough logistics details on two separate pickups, building numbers, floor levels, exact item counts, and gated-community access requirements — that was comprehensive and well-organized.
coaching_note: Jules never asked for the customer's concerns upfront (Section 2), never anchored pricing to typical range or personalized it (Section 4), and ended with a passive hand-off instead of asking plainly 'Would you like our help with your move?' and actually booking them (Section 7) — the call lacks the structure and closing discipline the script requires.
